35th report on the working of Rural Employment Generation Programme and Prime Minister’s Rozgar Yojana which was
presented to the Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of the Lok Sabha on 2nd May, 2000.

CHAPTER-I
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 4-5
 
4.         The Sub-Committee feels that recovery of pending cases should be expedited by fixing accountability at district
administration level also.  In addition the record of pending cases be computerised and updated at regular intervals.  There
should be time bound specific targets to be monitored at District level by District magistrates.
 
5.         The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government to explore ways and means for recovery of PMRY loans
under defaults, as delays occur in serving of notices and appearance in the Court.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The Office has been monitoring to improve/expedite the recovery of loan dues under the PMRY.  The State/UTs
have been requested to include in their existing Land Revenue Arrears Recovery Acts, recovery of loan arrears under
PMRY, so that these are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.  The State/UTs were requested to conduct joint recovery
drives.  A letter was written to State/UTs on 26.6.2000 reiterating the need to take necessary steps to improve recovery of
loan under the scheme.  A copy of the letter written to State/UTs on 26.6.2000 is enclosed for ready reference (Annexure
– III).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.  6             
 
The Sub-Committee observes that bankers generally raise their concern about the late communication of targets to
them from the Government.  For example, targets are being communicated in August/September wherein they are to be
achievable by March (end of financial year).  The Sub-Committee recommends that the targets for PMRY should be
communicated to Banks from the Government, well in time to avoid any kind of time constraint.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The basic target for the year 2000-2001 under the PMRY were communicated to State/UTs and to the RBI on
19.4.2000.  The additional targets under the scheme were communicated to the State/UTs and to the RBI on 16.6.2000. 
The RBI has been requested to convey the bank-wise target as early as possible in the light of the recommendation of the

Committee.  A copy of the letter written to the RBI in this regard is enclosed. (Annexure – II).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO. 7 & 11
 
7.         The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government that DICs should avoid disproportionate sponsoring of
applications under PMRY.  This act, in return, will minimise the pendency rate of applications.
 
11.       The Sub-Committee has noticed that DICs fail to complete the identification process well in advance.  As a matter
of fact, in place of transmission of applications to banks under PMRY, in a phased manner, they do the same in bunching.
 
The Sub-Committee, therefore, recommends that it has to be ensured that the flow of applications from DICs to
banks; take place in a phased manner and the practice of bunching of applications should be stopped.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The Office of the Dev. Commissioner(SSI), while communicating the annual target to the State/UTs prescribes a
quarterly schedule for sponsoring of applications by the District Task force Committees to banks.  A copy of the schedule
is enclosed for ready reference (Annexure – IV).  The State/UTs have been requested to issue necessary instructions to the
DICs to adhere to the schedule prescribed for sponsoring of applications to avoid disproportionate sponsoring of
applications to banks to avoid bunching of applications at the fag end of the year.  A copy of the letter issued to State/UTs
is enclosed. (Annexure – V)
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/ OBSERVATION NO. 8
 
The Sub-Committee observes that under PMRY, quality applications are not being sponsored to   banks.  As
regards this shortcoming, the Sub-Committee feels that Branch Managers should be involved actively in selecting the
beneficiaries and the activities.
           
ACTION TAKEN
 
The guidelines of the PMRY scheme provides for the inclusion of the lead bank and other participating banks as
the members of the district task force committees.  The subsequent guidelines also provide that all participating banks in a
district may participate in the district task force committee meetings on a rotational basis.  A copy of the letter is enclosed
(Annexure – VI).  The RBI vide Circular dated 19.11.96 has instructed to CMDs of all Indian Scheduled Commercial
Banks that banks can receive the applications directly and send them to the sponsoring agencies with their observations on
the viability and bankability of the project.  A copy of the letter is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure – VII)
 
            The RBI has been requested to reiterate the necessary instructions in view of the recommendation of the
Committee.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 9
 
As per the provisions made under PMRY, loans should be in the ratio of 50%, 30% and 20% in respect  of
industry, services and business sector.  During the course of the discussion, the Sub-Committee came to know that mostly
applications are received for business activities and applications regarding industry are few in numbers.  The Sub-
Committee feels that steps should be taken to ensure that the ratio of loans for all three activities are maintained according
to provisions contained in the Scheme.
 
 
 
ACTION TAKEN

            The State/UTs have been requested to sponsor more applications for industry sector in view of the fact that it has
more employment potential.  A copy of the letter issued to State/UTs is enclosed. (Annexure – V).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION  NO. 12
 
The Sub-Committee notes that PMRY Club is a novel idea.  As a result of implementation of this, majority of the
problems such as creation of assets, marketing arrangement and repayment of bank’s dues etc. will be easily overcome. 
The Sub-Committee, therefore, recommends that efforts should be taken to ensure that PMRY Clubs should be
encouraged to start its operation in all the prominent centres.
 
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The State/UTs have been requested to explore the possibility for starting the PMRY club in their States/UTs.  A
copy of the letter written to State/UTs is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure – V).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.13
 
The Sub-Committee notes with discontent that the reduction in disbursement as compared to loan amount applied
for has been dampening the spirit and enthusiasm of borrowers of PMRY.  So, the Sub-Committee impresses upon the
Government to take suitable corrective measures as regards the cases, the quantum of which is sizeable, where it is
presumed by bankers that borrowers are incapable to executing the projects or there is likelyhood of less demand in the
area due to saturation of activity and thus the loan applied for is reduced without following any yardstick.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The matter was discussed in the 10
th Meeting of High Powered Committee for the PMRY held on 22.3.2000 and it
was decided that banks may be advised by the RBI to adequately finance micro enterprises set up under the PMRY so that
they do not become unviable due to inadequate funds. The RBI has issued instructions to CMDs,  Indian Scheduled
Commercial Banks to assess properly the working capital need of the units to be set up under the scheme.  A copy of the
letter is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure – IX)
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.14
 
The Sub-Committee is unhappy to note that in several cases of PMRY loans, the disbursement is stopped or
delayed on unjustified/flimsy grounds.  Thus, the Sub-Committee recommends that suitable measures should be taken
concerning the stoppage/delay of disbursement of PMRY loans on such grounds.
 
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The RBI vide its letter dated 10.12.97 addressed to CMDs of all Indian Scheduled Commercial Banks has stated
that in several cases banks have delayed disbursement of loan on unjustified/flimsy grounds. A copy of the letter written
by the RBI is enclosed for ready reference (Annexure – X).  The RBI is requested to initiate action on the
recommendation of the committee. 
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.18
 
The Sub-Committee notes with discontent that till now banks are not very enthusiastic about projects under
PMRY.

ACTION TAKEN
 
            The finding of the committee has been communicated to the RBI.  A copy of the letter written to the RBI is
enclosed for ready reference.   (Annexure – II)
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.19 &  21
 
19.       The Sub-Committee feels that appropriate measures are still needed to generate awareness and educate the people
in remote and urban areas about the PMRY.
 
21.       The Sub-Committee observes that an orientation programme should be conducted by DIC for the target  groups at
Block/Taluka level to enlighten them about various viable activities.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            Central Govt. releases contingency funds to the State/UTs @ Rs.250/- per beneficiary.  The permitted expenditure
under the contingency funds include holding motivational campaigns, familiarisation programmes and preparation of
locally relevant project profiles.  Upto 1999-2000, Rs.2581.98 lakhs have been released to State/UTs as contingency
funds.
 
            The State/UTs have been requested to take necessary action on the recommendation of the Committee in this
regard.  A copy of the letter written to State/UTs is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure V).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 22
 
The Sub-Committee, through its discussion, came to know that Margin Money Scheme of REGP is in its nascent
stage and it will normally take some time until it stabilises and results are seen.
 
The Sub-Committee feels that concerted efforts should be made so that all bank branches will understand the
essence of the scheme.  Related to it, all regional offices should hold one day workshop at important/potential district
centres to explain the Scheme to the Branch Managers.  In addition, interaction sessions will be of immense help and that
should be arranged between KVIC officials, regional office functionaries of banks and grass-root functionaries at branch
level.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
a.         The KVIC regularly interacts with Bankers by holding quarterly review meetings, in addition to occasional Review
Meetings being held at the State level.
 
b.         The KVIC has also initiated action by conducting District/Regional/State level workshops on the Margin Money
Scheme, in which Bankers and concerned District/State level functionaries are actively involved.
 
c.         In order to make the interaction between the KVIC/KVIBs and the Bank functionaries effective, the controlling
offices of Banks have been advised to organise Workshops for Branch Managers and Regional Managers.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 23
 
The Sub-Committee feels that model proposals on illustrative rural industries should be prepared and circulated to 
bank branches for their guidance.  Nonetheless, while preparing these model proposals concerning REGP, industries
specific to a particular district, must be kept in mind.
 
ACTION TAKEN

a)         Model project profiles of some important village industries have been prepared by the KVIC which are under
process of circulation among the Bankers.
 
b)         Action has already been initiated for collecting lists of districts from each State/UTs, indicating District-wise
potential village industries.  Necessary communications in this regard has already been issued to the KVIC’s field offices
for collecting and submitting the information immediately.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 24
 
            The Sub-committee observes that concerning Margin Money Scheme, subsidy procedures are not properly
understood by Bank branches.  So, in the opinion of the Sub-Committee, model guidelines for subsidy claims should be
made available to Banks.  As a result, subsidy claims will not be rejected or returned for resubmission.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The KVIC has circulated details of the Margin Money Scheme to all Banks which includes procedure, formats for
submission of the Margin Money claims and as such the matter has been made amply clear to the Banks.  Further, during
the quarterly review meetings and District/Regional level workshops also such issues are being discussed.  In addition,
communications received from Banks for any clarification in this regard are promptly attended to by the KVIC and
disposed off on priority basis.
 
 
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 25
 
The Sub-Committee observes that relating to REGP, suitable advertisement pamphlets in English/Hindi/Local
languages must be printed and distributed to Bank branches for circulating them among the rural population.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            Action has already been taken in this regard by circulating English and Hindi versions of booklets on Margin
Money Scheme to Banks.  Moreover, the KVIC has also printed pamphlets on this scheme in various local languages and
sufficient copies have been made available to District Collectors in all States/UTs to distribute the same among the rural
entrepreneurs.  Posters in Hindi and English have also been printed and distributed.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 27
 
The Sub-Committee notes that Government should make the required efforts to make Banks more enthusiastic
about various programmes of Rural Employment Generation Programme.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            Time to time Government have requested the State Governments/UTs and Banks to make all possible efforts to
popularise REGP for its effective  implementation.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 30
 
The Sub-Committee recommends that Government should formulate programmes like Rural Entrepreneur
Development Programme (REDP) in order to equip the beneficiaries to take the benefits of Margin Money Scheme by
bringing suitable bankable projects to their notice.

ACTION TAKEN
 
The suggestion of the Committee will be kept in mind as and when some policy decision is taken in future.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 38
 
The Sub-Committee came to know that the employment generated by coir industry is by and large considered as
part time. Thus the Sub-Committee recommends that Government should ensure the implementation of various measures
for enhancing the number of days of work, so that the said employment becomes regular.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Employment generation in coir industry depends on the demand for coir products. The programmes envisaged
under Domestic Market Development and Export Promotion are aimed at developing the market of coir and coir products
in India and abroad. There has been an increasing trend in the domestic as well as international market for coir products,
as evidenced by the enhancement in domestic consumption and exports.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 39
 
The marketing and sale of coir products in India still require the acceleration. The Sub-Committee feels that
Government should augment the marketing and sales of coir products in the domestic market.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The following actions have been initiated  to augment the marketing and sales of  coir products in the domestic
market:-
 
1.
      Participation in Exhibitions in different parts of India.
 
2.
      Publicity on TV network and  in print media.
 
 
3.
      Rebate/domestic market assistance to increase the domestic market for coir and coir products.
 
4.
      Opening up the market in the North Eastern Region.
 
5.   Opening of sales outlets through Showrooms of Government/Govt. supported agencies.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 40
 
The Sub-Committee feels that for obtaining raw materials for coir industry at reasonable prices, Government
should ensure the establishment of adequate number of raw material banks in different areas. By this, there will be steady
assured supply of raw materials such as coir  fibre, coir yarn and dyes and chemicals etc. at reasonable prices.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Raw Material Banking is a commercial activity, however, the Coir Board is helping institutions/individuals to set
up Banks in coir clusters.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 41

The Sub-Committee  impresses upon the Government to augment the modernisation of extraction and processing
of fibres, development of coir machinery product development and diversification.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The Science and Technology activities are aimed  to augment the modernisation of extraction and processing of
fibre, development of coir machinery, product development and diversification. The Board also undertakes collaborative
research projects with other R&D Institutions, Universities etc. to accelerate R & D activities.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 43
 
Coir Board is extending financial assistance to coir units in the Brown Coir Fibre sector for setting up of new coir
units and also for modernisation/renovation of existing units. Under this scheme, the Sub-Committee feel that the financial
assistance of 25 per cent subject to the maximum of Rs. 1.00 lakh, being extended to coir units is meagre amount and it
needs to be enhanced at least by four to five times.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The Ministry has approved the revised financial assistance scheme vide letter No. 5(20)/96-Coir dated 7-4-99.
According to the revised scheme the quantum of financial assistance has been revised to Rs. 1.5 lakhs from Rs. 1 lakh and
the scope of the scheme has also been enlarged by including 8 new types of coir processing units.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 44
 
Hindustan Coir was established in the year 1968  with a view to mechanise the coir industry in a phased manner.
Thus Hindustan Coir is pioneering for introduction of gradual mechanisation of the manufacturing process and
development of the industry on modern lines. The Sub-Committee feels that Government should take necessary steps to
augment the production of this factory.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Action to provide necessary balancing equipments has been initiated to enhance productivity of the Hindustan Coir
Factory.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 46
 
The state of affairs of various Cooperative Societies and State owned Coir Cooperations are not much sound in
coir producing States, viz. Tamil Nadu Karnataka and Kerala. They, by and large, play an important role in providing
employment to large number of workers in the rural sector. The Sub-Committee urges upon the Government to make
efforts for making Cooperative Societies and State owned Coir Corporations strong in the  coir sector.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Government has approved the Integrated Coir Development Project to be implemented in Tamil Nadu at a total
cost of Rs. 1490.73 lakhs, in Karnataka at a total outlay of Rs. 465.48 lakhs, and in Kerala at a total cost of Rs. 4424.00
lakhs. These projects are aimed at modernising and strengthening the Cooperatives in coir sector in the above states. The
State owned Coir Corporations although are within the ambit of the concerned State Government.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 47

The Sub-Committee feels that Government should work at its best, in this present scenario of globalization and
liberalization, so that the cooperative sector and private sector in coir industry work side by side.

All out efforts are being made to spread the message of the effect of globalization and liberalization in the coir
industry. The procedure for export of coir has been liberalised. The Minimum Export Policy has also been recently
amended in view of the liberalization and the globalization.
 
CHAPTER-II
 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATINS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN
VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLY
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 1
 
In view of price-rise and inflation, the project cost limit under PMRY for the Services/Industry/Business sector,
does not seem to be appropriate.  The Sub-Committee accordingly recommends that a review of the project cost limit for
Services/Industry/Business sector should be undertaken to adjust it suitably with the present cost of Rupees.  The ceiling
for project cost/loan should be realistic, taking into account the activity and location of the project.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The Cabinet approved modifications in the parameters of the PMRY on 24.12.98.  The modified parameters are
under implementation since 1.4.1999. The modified parameters include enhancement in the project cost for self
employment ventures to be set up under industry and service sector from Rs.1 lakh to Rs.2 lakhs.  The project cost for self
employment ventures to be set up under business sector continues to Rs.1 lakh.  A copy of the modified guidelines is
enclosed for ready reference.  (Annexure – I)
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 20
 
            The Sub-Committee feels that necessary measures are required to check the instances where the loans/subsidy are
being utilized for the purpose other than the purposes for which these are granted.
 
ACTION TAKEN REPORT:
 
            The Office of the Dev. Commissioner(SSI) vide letter dated 11.5.99 addressed to all State/UTs and to the RBI has
forwarded the views of M/o Law & Justice that cases can be filed against those borrowers who mis-utilise the loan

RECOMMENDATION NO. 26
 
The Sub-Committee recommends that monitoring cells should be set up at Regional/Zonal offices to monitor the
progress of REGP regularly.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
In order to monitor the implementation of the Margin Money Scheme and also guide the potential entrepreneurs,
State Level Task Forces on the MMS have been constituted under the Chairmanship of the Commissioner of Industries of
the respective State/UT.  This Task Force includes Chairman of State Level Bankers Committee (SLBC) and Managing
Director of State Apex Cooperative Bank, Chairman of RRBs etc.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 28
 
The Sub-Committee notes with discontent that funds for Rural Employment Generation Programme including
District Special  Employment Programme and RPDS Block Development Programme are still to be disbursed and
apparently making the Scheme dysfunctional.  The Sub-Committee recommends that Government should take all
necessary steps to overcome such situation and ascertain the continuous flow of funds by the KVIC.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The District Special Employment Programme and RPDS Blocks Development Programme of the KVIC have been
merged in its normal programme of the REGP w.e.f. 1.4.1999 and as such no separate funds are allocated.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 32
 
The Sub-Committee feels that requisite amendments in  KVIC’s notification should be brought out, concerning the
population criteria in Margin Money Scheme, as there are some villages which are classified as Municipal Villages in
Kerala State.
 
ACTION  TAKEN 
 
Since there  are some States like Kerala, where density of population is high and characteristic of rural area is
slowly fading away, certain amendments to the KVIC’s Act, to accommodate larger population may be appropriate.  The
Government amended KVIC Act in this regard vide Notification dated  27.10.1994 and the definition of Village is as
under:-
 
“The area comprises any village and includes area comprised any town, the population of which does not exceed
20,000 or such other figures as the Central Government may specify from time to time”.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 34
 
The Sub-Committee notes that programmes for the KVIC sector should be finalised in advance, so that the State
Boards can prepare their action plan in accordance with the guidelines of the KVIC.  The Sub-Committee also views that
there is necessity to ensure the confidence of entrepreneurs about the continuation of the programme and easy availability
of funds.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
Regarding Margin Money Scheme, the RBI has already provided necessary code Numbers to Village Industries

RECOMMENDATION NO. 35
 
The Sub-Committee came to know that Khadi sector has been providing more employment opportunities
especially for the women folk in rural areas.  Some of the State Governments have been providing incentive wages for
spinners and weavers.  The Sub-Committee thus feels that Central Government should also provide such wage incentives

ACTION TAKEN
 
The wage rate/incentive of Khadi Sector is regulated by the provision made in the Khadi cost chart.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 45
 
The Sub-Committee came to know that usual annual average stock holding of coir products is of Rs. 15 Crore. The
Sub-Committee feels that adequate measures should be taken by Government to clear the stock holding of coir products.
 
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The measures taken for domestic market development and export promotion are expected to increase the demand
for coir and coir and coir products.

RECOMMENDATION NO. 2
 
The Sub-Committee notes that under PMRY, there is subsidy ceiling of Rs.7,500/.  The Sub-Committee is of the
view that the practice of subsidy ceiling may be dispensed with and instead 15 per cent subsidy may be made, admissible
for all quantum of loan amount.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The rate of subsidy has since been revised for the NE States.  It is @ 15 per cent of the project cost subject to a
ceiling of Rs.15,000/- per beneficiary.  It has been decided in the 10
th Meeting of High powered Committee for PMRY
that the ceiling on subsidy may also be raised for weaker sections i.e. SC/STs, ex-servicemen, physically disabled persons
and women and also for the States/UTs of J&K, Sikkim, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.  This could be
implemented only after approval from the Cabinet.
 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
The Committee  hopes  that   approval of Cabinet  would  be obtained  at the earliest and it would be implemented
expeditiously.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.3
 
The Sub-Committee observes that the recovery under PMRY is far from satisfaction.  The Sub-Committee,
accordingly, is of the view that the recovery process of PMRY loans at bank level can be strengthened by creating District

ACTION TAKEN
 
            The RBI has been requested to initiate necessary action on the recommendations of the Committee.  A copy of the
communication sent to RBI is enclosed.  (Annexure – II). 
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
The Committee recommends that the Government may pursue the matter with RBI for an early implementation of
the recommendation.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.  10
 
The general view is that viability aspects of proposals are ignored by DICs while sponsoring the  applications
under PMRY.  The Sub-Committee recommends that DICs should go thoroughly into the details of each and every
proposal including spot verification, technical feasibility and financial viability.
In this connection, the Sub-Committee further recommends that the plea of helplessness from DICs, for want of
staff should not be taken as an excuse.
 
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The issue was discussed in the 10
th Meeting of the High powered Committee for the PMRY held on 22.3.2000 
and it was decided that State/UTs may be requested to instruct to the DICs to identify viable projects in their respective
districts and prepare project profiles for the guidelines of the prospective entrepreneurs under the PMRY.  In addition
project profiles prepared by the SISIs used by various financial institutions (FIs) and similar agencies can also utilised.  A
copy of the letter written to all State/UTs is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure – VIII).
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            The Committee feels that DICs will have to play a pro-active role. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
recommendation that DICs should go thoroughly into every proposal. DICs  should invariably prepare project profiles for
assistance of  prospective entrepreneurs.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 15
 
The Sub-Committee strongly recommends that necessary steps should be taken by the bank management to do
away with the prevailing psychosis of bank branches that if they start sanctioning the cases of PMRY on regular basis then
pending cases of non-performing banks will be thrust upon them.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The finding of the committee has been communicated to the RBI.  A copy of the letter written to RBI is enclosed
for ready reference. (Annexure – II)
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            The Committee feels that RBI needs to do a thorough review of the system.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 16  &  17
 
16.       The Sub-Committee strongly recommends that RBI’s guidelines for disposing of applications under PMRY within
the time-period of thirty days must be adhered to by banks.  Concerning it, the responsibilities should be fixed to
undertake needful corrective measures.

            The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation in this regard and feels that RBI should regularly monitor this

RECOMMENDATION NO. 31
 
The Sub-Committee recommends that necessary initiatives should be taken, so that NABARD’S  participation in

The KVIC regularly inter-acts with the NABARD on various issues, where NABARD can give
suggestions/guidance.  As an example, before engaging Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Cooperative Banks under the

of Margin Money Scheme.

            The  Committee  is   of the view that  enhancement of  NABARD’s  participation in KVIC’s Margin Money
Scheme in respect of refinance facility   should   be  ensured .

Over a period of time, more than 25% of the Khadi units have become sick due to various reasons.  There is no
programme with the KVIC for rehabilitating the sick units.  The Sub-Committee thus recommends that revival of sick
units should become a continuous programme alongwith the establishment of new units.  Moreover, the continuous
monitoring of the functioning of the old units will ensure the recovery of dues and continuous employment in rural areas.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The KVIC has already formulated guidelines for revitalizing sick Khadi institutions (copy enclosed) Annexure
XIII.
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
The guidelines may be implemented at the earliest. Implementation of  guidelines for  revitalizing  sick khadi
institutions  should be monitored   properly .   The Committee   reiterates  the recommendation that revival    of sick units 
should become a  continuous  process alongwith  the  establishment of   new units.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 36
 
The Sub-Committee came to know that KVIBs have been implementing Margin Money Scheme of the KVIC,
wherein the scheme envisages loan portion of the project cost to be met from Consortium Bank  Credit (CBC) sources and
margin money from the KVIB budgetary sources.  The Sub-Committee recommends that KVIBs should be better
equipped and strengthened so that they can become the catalysts of rural industries in the country.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The KVIC impress upon the State Governments to strengthen the infrastructure facilities of State KVI Boards so
that they can implement the programme in a more effective manner.
 
In order to implement the REGP/Margin Money Scheme, the KVIC had also placed Margin Money Grant with
State/UT KVI Boards in advance, so that the programme can be implemented without any delay.  However, it is observed
that due to weak infrastructure facilities some of the State/UT KVI Boards are not in a position to utilise such grants made
available to them even after a lapse of considerable time.  As far as projects under Margin Money Scheme are concerned,
the State/UT KVI Boards are empowered to recommend projects by ensuring its techno-economic viability without
awaiting for the prior approval from the KVIC.
 
 
COMMENT/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            It is unfortunate that funds are not being utilized  due to  lack  of infrastructure facilities. Central Govt. should take
up the matter with all state/UT Govts. for improving infrastructure facilities.
 
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 37
 
The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government that more importance should be given for marketing of the
goods produced by KVI sector.  This will facilitate the expansion of rural industries by providing linkages.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The KVIC has already launched common brand names for selected village industries products.
 
COMMENTSOBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            The Committee is  not satisfied   with the  steps taken so far  for  marketing  of goods  produced by KVI Sector

other commercial  organizations  to promote  goods  in the market    and earn recognition.    The Committee reiterates  its

RECOMMENDATION NO.42
 
            The Sub-Committee came to know that existing Co-operativisation Scheme was approved in the Eight Plan period.
The quantum of assistance allotted for managerial subsidy is not enough to appoint managerial personnel in the societies.
In addition, the cost of machines proposed under equipment assistance is not updated. Some of the machines could not be
purchased at the cost mentioned in the Scheme. The updated machines for automatic spinning, semi-automatic looms,
curled coir and rubberised coir products are not included in this Scheme.
            Hence, the Sub-Committee is of the opinion that the quantum of assistance should be revised according to the
prevailing marketing rate and 100 per cent cost should be provided under this scheme.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The Scheme of cooperativisation is being evaluated to take a decision on its continuance.

            Evaluation of the Cooperativisation scheme may be completed at the earliest. In case it is decided not to continue
the scheme, alternative   steps may be taken to provide assistance for managerial subsidy. In such a situation, the quantum
of assistance may be fixed as per the prevailing market rate.
